headline: 1.27mn students: HSC and equivalent results published today
summary: Results will be announced at 11:00am, with students able to check their marks via websites, SMS, and educational institutions.
details: The results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published today. More than 12.70 lakh examinees took part in these exams.
The results will be formally announced at 11:00am in the meeting room of the Secondary and Higher Education Division, Ministry of Education.
Students can check their results simultaneously through their educational institutions, designated websites, and SMS.
Online results are available at https://eduboardresults.gov.bd and https://educationboardresults.gov.bd using roll and registration numbers.
Students can also receive their results instantly by sending an SMS to 16140 from any mobile operator in the prescribed format.
Applications for re-scrutiny or reassessment of answer scripts will start from November 1 for students dissatisfied with their results.
Students can apply online for reassessment until November 7, with detailed instructions available on the respective education boards' websites.
caption:
Over 1.27 million students are waiting for their HSC results today!

The results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published today. More than 12.70 lakh examinees took part in these exams.

The results will be formally announced at 11:00am in the meeting room of the Secondary and Higher Education Division, Ministry of Education.

Students can check their results simultaneously through their educational institutions, designated websites, and SMS.

Online results are available at https://eduboardresults.gov.bd and https://educationboardresults.gov.bd using roll and registration numbers.

Students can also receive their results instantly by sending an SMS to 16140 from any mobile operator in the prescribed format.

Applications for re-scrutiny or reassessment of answer scripts will start from November 1 for students dissatisfied with their results.

Students can apply online for reassessment until November 7, with detailed instructions available on the respective education boards' websites.

headline_marked: Govt: [[No third country discussed]] during PM's official visit to Japan
headline: Govt: No third country discussed during PM's official visit to Japan
summary: State Minister Humaiun Kobir denies claims that national interests were compromised, stressing that talks focused on bilateral economic ties.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir clarified that no third country was mentioned during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s recent official visit to Japan.
The Minister emphasized that the discussions were strictly bilateral, focusing on economic relations and strategic cooperation between Bangladesh and Japan.
The two nations agreed to upgrade the BIG-B initiative to 'BIG-B for Shared Prosperity' to tackle global supply chain risks and technological advances.
Humaiun Kobir responded to concerns raised by Opposition Leader and Jamaat Ameer Shafiqur Rahman regarding the Matarbari deep-sea port and national sovereignty.
He urged Jamaat-e-Islami to read the joint statement issued after the visit, denying allegations that Bangladesh had been 'sold'.
On Japanese loans, the Minister stated that Bangladesh would only accept investments with affordable interest rates and favorable terms that align with national interests.
He assured that the government would act with transparency and accountability, noting that any sensitive issues would be discussed in parliament.
caption:
Did Bangladesh compromise its sovereignty in Japan? The government says absolutely not.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir clarified that no third country was mentioned during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s recent official visit to Japan.

The Minister emphasized that the discussions were strictly bilateral, focusing on economic relations and strategic cooperation between Bangladesh and Japan.

The two nations agreed to upgrade the BIG-B initiative to 'BIG-B for Shared Prosperity' to tackle global supply chain risks and technological advances.

Humaiun Kobir responded to concerns raised by Opposition Leader and Jamaat Ameer Shafiqur Rahman regarding the Matarbari deep-sea port and national sovereignty.

He urged Jamaat-e-Islami to read the joint statement issued after the visit, denying allegations that Bangladesh had been 'sold'.

On Japanese loans, the Minister stated that Bangladesh would only accept investments with affordable interest rates and favorable terms that align with national interests.

He assured that the government would act with transparency and accountability, noting that any sensitive issues would be discussed in parliament.

#Bangladesh #Japan #Diplomacy #ForeignPolicy #BilateralTies

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, bdnews24.com
